newsitem.title: USA: Conrail head speaks to workers about future.
newsitem.headline: Conrail head speaks to workers about future.

text.p: Conrail Inc. Chief Executive Officer David LeVan spoke to thousands of railroad employees on Wednesday and echoed their insecurities after the apparent collapse of the company's planned merger with CSX Corp.
"This is a very unpleasant task... Even the CEO has insecurities about the future," LeVan said via satellite television beamed to several locations.
Shortly after LeVan began speaking, reporters were escorted from the hotel meeting room where employees were gathered in Conrail's home city to view the telecast.
Conrail workers said after the meeting that Le Van appeared crestfallen.

They said their own futures appeared highly uncertain in the wake of Conrail's decision Monday to renegotiate its agreement with CSX, thus setting the stage for a division of Philadelphia-based Conrail between CSX and rival bidder Norfolk Southern Corp.
"He seemed like he had been run over by a truck," said Conrail union clerk Pat Newcomb, referring to LeVan. "But he gave us some straight answers, as much as he could," he said.
Workers said LeVan had told them CSX and Norfolk would have a "moral obligation" to hire them in any restructured rail system, though that obligation would not be legal.
Conrail issued its statement Monday on renegotiating the planned merger with CSX, first announced in October.
Norfolk Southern, pursuing a higher bid for Conrail, was able in January to block Conrail shareholder approval of the proposed merger with CSX.
Conrail on Monday said it would negotiate a new agreement with CSX to bring shareholders $115 a share -- equal to Norfolk Southern's $10.3 billion bid -- as soon as possible.
